title: catalyst-week-company-alignment-brief-v0-1
body:
Purpose

This is the working brief for Catalyst Week: a condensed, cross-functional alignment sprint intended to calibrate exec priorities, finalize the company-level OKR draft for Q2–Q3 2026, and produce an all-hands narrative and comms plan. This doc captures proposed OKRs, talking points for the exec update, a lightweight all-hands agenda, communication owners, risk areas, and next steps. Use as the single source for the week-of runbook; comments and edits encouraged (track changes in Confluence page linked above).

Context and constraints
- Company stage: Growth into larger enterprise accounts, rolling Dedicated and Private GTM while maintaining hosted API velocity.
- Constraints: recruiting bandwidth limited in engineering, Dedicated capacity rollout timeline (target beta in May), regulatory sales cycles lengthening in EMEA.
- Primary ask: produce a short, concrete set of company-level OKRs that reflect serving/runtime reliability, cost-per-token improvements, and initial enterprise adoption metrics so product and GTM can align Q2 hiring and sales plays.

High-level outcomes for Catalyst Week (success criteria)
1) Execs agree on 3–5 company-level OKRs with measurable leading and lagging indicators.
2) All-hands deck draft ready with clear asks (what teams should prioritize) and a short demo/roadmap highlight.
3) Comms plan (email, blog, Slack, customer outreach) signed off and scheduled.
4) Risk register and contingency playbooks for top 3 operational risks created.

Proposed company-level OKR draft (company-level, keep concise)
Objective A: Ensure inference reliability and predictable SLAs for early enterprise customers\- Key Result A1: Achieve 99.95% uptime for hosted API across primary regions (rolling 30d).\- Key Result A2: Reduce median P99 request latency for production embeddings workloads by 20% vs baseline (baseline measured Feb 2026).\- Key Result A3: Complete Dedicated beta onboarding for 3 pilot customers with committed SLA response times and signed security assessments.

Objective B: Improve inference unit economics to enable sustainable hosted growth\- Key Result B1: Reduce average token cost (hosted) by 18% via batching, caching, and quantization improvements across 3 model families.\- Key Result B2: Increase percent of requests served from cache/prefix optimizations to 25% across API traffic.

Objective C: Strengthen product-led adoption and developer experience\- Key Result C1: Increase active API developers (30-day active) by 35% through quickstarts, template apps, and reduced time-to-first-response.\- Key Result C2: Publish 4 reference apps and 6 SDK updates with improved onboarding docs and sample prompts.

Notes on OKR framing and measurement
- Keep OKRs outcome-focused; implementation tactics belong in team plans.
- Measurement owners should be assigned this week (see owner column below).
- For enterprise pilot tracking, include signed security questionnaire and initial usage patterns (onboarding checklist).

Draft exec update talking points (5–7 minute segment)
1) Opening (CEO): one-sentence thesis tying market shift from model ownership to serving; why Redwood’s product posture is differentiated.
2) Quick snapshot: three bullets — uptime trend, cost-per-token improvement preview, Dedicated beta status.
3) Major asks: prioritization of SRE/resourcing for SLAs, commitment from product for two landing pages (Dedicated + Private), and GTM for three enterprise pilots.
4) Risks & mitigations: recruiting lag, capacity surge handling, and enterprise procurement cycles; each with one-line mitigation.
5) Close with tangible outcomes expected by next all-hands (metrics owners and dates).

All-hands agenda (30–40 minutes total)
- 0:00–0:03 Intro and context (CEO)
- 0:03–0:08 Product highlight: Serving runtime improvements + demo (Engineering lead)
- 0:08–0:14 Ops & reliability update (SRE lead)
- 0:14–0:20 Dedicated beta and customer stories (Solutions Eng / CS)
- 0:20–0:28 Exec asks and company OKR preview (CEO + COO)
- 0:28–0:35 Q&A (moderated)
- 0:35–0:40 Shoutouts and closing

Pre-reads and prep (who needs to deliver what)
- Product: 1 slide with one-line status on runtime/compilation improvements + before/after perf numbers (owner: Maya Chen)
- SRE: 1 slide with uptime, incident trend, three mitigations (owner: Daniel O'Neill)
- GTM: 1 slide summarizing Dedicated beta pipeline and next three customers to pilot (owner: Arjun Patel)
- CS/SE: 1 quick case note from pilot customer (owner: Priya Rao)
- Communications: drafted all-hands email and blog outline (owner: Sofia Martinez)

Communications plan (timeline and channels)
- Internal: All-hands (Day 0), follow-up summary email + Confluence with Q&A (Day 0 + Day 1).
- External: Short product blog announcing performance milestones and Dedicated beta call for pilots (Day 3 after internal sign-off).
- Customer outreach: targeted emails to top 20 prospects in pipeline (Sales + SE) within 5 business days.

Risk register (top 3 risks, owner, mitigation)
1) Risk: SLA miss during Dedicated pilot spike.
   Owner: Daniel O'Neill
   Mitigation: Burst capacity policy enabled, pre-warm for pilot windows, runbook for emergency fallback to lower-cost model variant.
2) Risk: Cost improvements don't materialize in measured traffic mix.
   Owner: Maya Chen
   Mitigation: Rapid evals per model family, rollback triggers for quantization if quality drops, dedicated eval suites for critical prompts.
3) Risk: Messaging leaks causing premature customer expectations.
   Owner: Sofia Martinez
   Mitigation: Tighten comms approval flow, embargo list for pilot customers, single-source product messaging doc.

Open questions for execs (to resolve during Catalyst Week)
- What is the accept/reject threshold for aggressive quantization tradeoffs (quality vs cost)? Who signs off?
- Prioritization: Hire for infra/SRE vs. product performance engineers — what timeline and headcount commit?
- Dedicated beta: list of must-have security docs before an external pilot vs nice-to-have.

Immediate next steps (this week)
- Today: Collect slide drafts from owners by EOD (owners listed above).
- Day -2 before all-hands: Draft email and blog copy for exec review (Sofia).
- Day 0 (Catalyst week kickoff): Exec review session to finalize OKRs and comms (time TBD).
- Post-event: Publish OKR sheet and assign measurement owners; create tracking dashboard in internal metrics.

Appendix: suggested metrics owners and contact info
- Uptime & incidents: Daniel O'Neill (daniel.o@redwood.ai)
- Latency profiling: Maya Chen (maya.c@redwood.ai)
- Cost/unit economics: Arjun Patel (arjun.p@redwood.ai)
- GTM and pilot pipeline: Priya Rao (priya.r@redwood.ai)

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally concise; the goal is to surface a concrete set of company OKRs and an executable all-hands with clear owners.
- Please add comments inline on Confluence rather than editing this file directly to preserve versioning.
- Finalization goal: sign-off by Exec team by EOD March 12, 2026 so comms can go live the week of March 15.

Revision history
- v0-1 2026-01-12: initial seed and owner list (Sofia)
- v0-2 2026-02-18: OKR refinement and SRE inputs (Daniel, Maya)
- v0-3 2026-03-05: updated timelines and added comms checklist (Sofia)
